c1-gen-0061: Hagar had fled into the wilderness, and the LORD spoke to her by a spring of water. Let's read Genesis 16:13 together.
c2-gen-0016: Isaac was born when Abraham was one hundred years old, and Sarah spoke about what God had done. Let's look at Genesis 21:6 and 7 together.
c2-gen-0017: The water in the skin was gone, and Hagar sat apart from the boy and wept. Let's read Genesis 21:17 and 19.
c2-gen-0018: Rebekah's family wanted her to stay at least ten days, so they asked Rebekah herself. Let's hear her in Genesis 24:57 and 58.
c2-gen-0019: That evening, as the camels came near, Isaac was out in the field. Let's open Genesis 24:63 and 67.
c2-gen-0020: The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's men over Esek and Sitnah, and then came a third well. Let's read Genesis 26:20, 21, and 22.
c3-gen-0001: At the well, Abraham's servant asked the LORD for a sign, and Rebekah did exactly what he had asked. Let's turn to Genesis 24:12, 24:14, and 24:27.
c3-gen-0002: God promised to make a nation of Hagar's son too, and later He spoke a big promise to Isaac at Beersheba. Let's read Genesis 21:12, 21:13, and 26:24.
c1-exo-0021: While Moses was on the mountain, the people gathered to Aaron and asked for gods to go before them. Let's check Exodus 32:1.
c2-exo-0014: Aaron took the gold and fashioned it with an engraving tool, and then Moses confronted him. Let's hear Aaron's version in Exodus 32:4 and 32:24.
c2-exo-0015: Moses went back to the LORD and confessed the people's sin. Let's read Exodus 32:31 and 32.
c2-exo-0016: Moses came down from Mount Sinai with his face shining, and the people were afraid to come near. Let's dig into Exodus 34:30 and 33.
c2-exo-0017: When Moses saw what the people were doing, his anger burned at the foot of the mountain. Let's read Exodus 32:19 and 34:1.
c2-exo-0018: Moses asked the LORD who would go with him, and the LORD promised His Presence. Read Exodus 33:14 and 15 with me.
c3-exo-0001: Moses prayed, "Please, show me Your glory." Let's read Exodus 33:18, 19, and 22.
c3-exo-0002: Moses pleaded for the people and asked the LORD to remember His oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Let's go to Exodus 32:13, 34:6, and 34:7.
c1-jos-0015: All Israel crossed the Jordan and camped in a new place, with twelve stones taken from the river. Let's read Joshua 4:19 and 20.
c2-jos-0003: Joshua knew children would one day ask, "What do these stones mean to you?" Let's look closely at Joshua 4:6 and 7.
c2-jos-0004: Achan confessed to taking a Babylonian garment, silver, and a wedge of gold. Let's read Joshua 7:20 and 21.
c2-jos-0005: The Gibeonites wanted Israel to believe they had come from a far country. Let's look at Joshua 9:12 and 13 together.
c2-jos-0006: At Gibeon the LORD cast down large hailstones, and Joshua spoke to the LORD in the sight of Israel. Let's read Joshua 10:11, 12, and 14.
c2-jos-0007: Joshua said he and his house would serve the LORD, and the people said they would serve Him too. Let's open Joshua 24:15, 18, and 19.
c3-jos-0001: In Joshua 4 the stones answered a question, and in Joshua 24 Joshua set up a large stone under the oak. Let's read Joshua 4:6, 24:26, and 24:27.
c3-jos-0002: Between the Jordan stones and Joshua's call to choose, the Gibeonites showed up with worn-out supplies. Let's turn to Joshua 4:24, 9:14, and 24:15.
c1-1sa-0010: Hannah prayed in her heart at the tabernacle; her lips moved, but no sound came out. Let's read First Samuel 1:13 and 14.
c2-1sa-0001: The LORD remembered Hannah, and she bore a son and named him Samuel. Let's check First Samuel 1:20 together.
c2-1sa-0002: When Samuel was weaned, Hannah brought him to Eli, thankful that the LORD had granted her petition. Let's read First Samuel 1:27 and 28.
c2-1sa-0003: Young Samuel ministered before the LORD in a linen ephod, and his mother came up every year with her husband. Let's dig into First Samuel 2:18 and 19.
c2-1sa-0004: Hannah's song begins with this: no one is holy like the LORD. Let's read First Samuel 2:2, 7, and 8.
c2-1sa-0005: First Samuel sets Eli's sons and the child Samuel side by side. Read First Samuel 2:12 and 26 with me.
c3-1sa-0001: The LORD called, and young Samuel answered, "Speak, for Your servant hears." Let's read First Samuel 3:10 and 19.
c3-1sa-0002: Elkanah went up every year to worship, back before the word of the LORD grew rare. Let's go to First Samuel 1:3, 3:1, and 3:21.
c1-1sa-0011: Kish sent his son Saul out with one of the servants on a search. Let's read First Samuel 9:3.
c2-1sa-0006: Samuel's sons did not walk in his ways, and the elders wanted a king. Let's look closely at First Samuel 8:5 and 8:20.
c2-1sa-0007: The elders' request for a king displeased Samuel, so he prayed to the LORD. Let's read First Samuel 8:6 and 7.
c2-1sa-0008: At Mizpah, Saul was chosen, but when they looked for him, he could not be found! Let's look at First Samuel 10:21 and 22 together.
c2-1sa-0009: The people shouted, "Long live the king!" but some rebels grumbled about Saul. Let's read First Samuel 10:24 and 27.
c2-1sa-0010: Saul waited seven days, and when Samuel did not come, he offered the burnt offering himself. Let's open First Samuel 13:8, 9, and 14.
c3-1sa-0003: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed hold of him, and something tore. Let's read First Samuel 15:27 and 28.
c3-1sa-0004: Saul explained himself twice, once before a battle and once after the battle with Amalek. Let's turn to First Samuel 13:12, 15:21, and 15:22.
c1-1sa-0012: David came home from striking down the Philistine, and the women came out singing and dancing. Let's read First Samuel 18:6 and 7.
c2-1sa-0011: After the women's song, Saul eyed David from that day forward. Let's check First Samuel 18:9 and 11.
c2-1sa-0012: Jonathan worked out a secret signal for David using arrows. Let's read First Samuel 20:21 and 22.
c2-1sa-0013: In the cave at En Gedi, David's men urged him to act against Saul. Let's dig into First Samuel 24:4 and 5.
c2-1sa-0014: David and Abishai crept into Saul's camp while everyone slept. Let's read First Samuel 26:11, 12, and 16.
c2-1sa-0015: The valiant men of Jabesh Gilead brought back Saul and his sons and buried their bones under the tamarisk tree. Read First Samuel 31:11 and 13 with me.
c3-1sa-0005: Jonathan loved David as his own soul, and the two made a covenant. Let's read First Samuel 18:3 and 20:42.
c3-1sa-0006: In the cave, David spared Saul and called out to him. Let's go to First Samuel 24:12, 24:15, and 26:10.
c1-ezr-0001: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD stirred up his spirit, and Cyrus sent out a proclamation. Let's read Ezra 1:1 and 2.
c2-ezr-0001: The returned exiles gathered in Jerusalem, afraid of the peoples around them. Let's look closely at Ezra 3:3 and 6.
c2-ezr-0002: The foundation was laid at last, and the priests and Levites sang responsively. Let's read Ezra 3:11.
c2-ezr-0003: Ezra came up to Jerusalem from Babylon during the reign of Artaxerxes. Let's look at Ezra 7:6 together.
c2-ezr-0004: When the base was laid, many people shouted aloud, but many others wept with a loud voice. Let's read Ezra 3:12 and 13.
c2-ezr-0005: In the reign of King Darius, the work was finally finished. Let's open Ezra 6:15, 16, and 22.
c3-ezr-0001: Ezra 7 credits the hand of God for Ezra's success and his safe journey. Let's read Ezra 7:6, 9, and 10.
c3-ezr-0002: Ezra's story opens with the LORD stirring the spirit of Cyrus, and it closes with another king's heart turned. Let's turn to Ezra 1:1 and 6:22.
c1-neh-0001: Nehemiah asked for mercy "in the sight of this man." Let's read all the way to the end of Nehemiah 1:11.
c2-neh-0001: Men from Judah told Nehemiah that the survivors were in distress and Jerusalem's gates were burned. Let's read Nehemiah 1:3 and 4.
c2-neh-0002: The people mourned when they heard the words of the Law, but their leaders said the day was holy. Let's check Nehemiah 8:9 and 10.
c2-neh-0003: Sanballat mocked the builders, and Tobiah joked that a fox could break down their wall. Let's read Nehemiah 4:3 and 6.
c2-neh-0004: Nehemiah went out at night to view the broken walls and told no one. Let's dig into Nehemiah 2:12, 15, and 18.
c2-neh-0005: Ezra read the Law from morning until midday, and everyone listened closely. Let's read Nehemiah 8:3 and 5.
c3-neh-0001: Nehemiah faced the king's question and, later, enemies plotting an attack. Read Nehemiah 2:4 and 4:9 with me.
c3-neh-0002: Nehemiah told the builders, "Our God will fight for us," and the wall was finished in fifty-two days. Let's read Nehemiah 4:20, 6:15, and 6:16.
c1-ezr-0002: Ezra heard the report, tore his garment and robe, and sat astonished until the evening sacrifice. Let's go to Ezra 9:3 and 5.
c2-ezr-0006: Ezra began his prayer too ashamed to lift up his face to God. Let's read Ezra 9:6.
c2-neh-0006: Nehemiah came back and found a room in the courts of God's house set up for Tobiah. Let's look closely at Nehemiah 13:7 and 8.
c2-neh-0007: Merchants kept hauling loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. Let's read Nehemiah 13:19.
c2-ezr-0007: Ezra says that for a little while, grace had been shown to them in their bondage. Let's look at Ezra 9:8 and 9 together.
c2-neh-0008: The fathers acted proudly and hardened their necks, and then the prayer turns: "But You are God." Let's read Nehemiah 9:16 and 17.
c3-neh-0003: The people asked God not to let all their trouble seem small before Him. Let's open Nehemiah 9:32 and 33.
c3-ezr-0003: Ezra admitted that no one could stand before God because of their guilt. Let's read Ezra 9:13 and 15.
c1-psa-0018: The psalmist lifts his eyes to the hills and asks where his help comes from. Let's turn to Psalm 121:1 and 2.
c2-psa-0008: The psalmist says he will praise God, and he tells us why. Let's read Psalm 139:14.
c2-psa-0009: In Psalm 51, the psalmist asks God to wash him. Let's check Psalm 51:10.
c2-psa-0010: The psalmist asks to be purged with hyssop and washed. Let's read Psalm 51:7.
c2-psa-0011: God promises to instruct and teach His people in the way they should go. Let's dig into Psalm 32:8 and 9.
c2-psa-0012: The LORD is my refuge and my fortress, and He covers you with His feathers. Let's read Psalm 91:2 and 4.
c3-psa-0002: "Where can I go from Your Spirit?" the psalmist asks. Read Psalm 139:7, 9, and 10 with me.
c3-psa-0003: Psalm 51 says what God will not despise, and Psalm 32 shows one man coming to God that way. Let's read Psalm 32:5, 51:16, and 51:17.
c1-psa-0019: Psalm 136 retells God's works from creation, through the wilderness, all the way to the land. Let's go to Psalm 136:1 and 26.
c2-psa-0013: Psalm 78 promises not to hide God's works from the children. Let's read Psalm 78:4 and 6.
c2-psa-0014: Israel's fathers were few in number, wandering from nation to nation. Let's look closely at Psalm 105:14 and 15.
c2-psa-0015: After what happened at Horeb, God said He would destroy His people. Let's read Psalm 106:23.
c2-psa-0016: The people remembered that God was their rock and their Redeemer, but there was a problem. Let's look at Psalm 78:35, 36, and 37 together.
c2-psa-0017: God remembers His covenant forever, made with Abraham and confirmed to Isaac and Jacob. Let's read Psalm 105:8 and 11.
c3-psa-0004: God took David from the sheepfolds to shepherd His people. Let's open Psalm 78:70, 71, and 72.
c3-psa-0005: God heard His people's cry and remembered His covenant for their sake. Let's read Psalm 78:38, 106:44, and 106:45.
c1-pro-0018: Proverbs pictures Wisdom as a woman calling out. Let's turn to Proverbs 1:20 and 21.
c2-pro-0008: Wisdom warns that the turning away of the simple will slay them. Let's read Proverbs 1:32 and 33.
c2-pro-0009: Wisdom tells her hearers to take her instruction instead of silver. Let's check Proverbs 8:11.
c2-pro-0010: Charm is deceitful and beauty is passing. Let's read Proverbs 31:30.
c2-pro-0011: Wisdom warns that those who rejected her will seek her and not find her. Let's dig into Proverbs 1:28 and 8:17.
c2-pro-0012: Proverbs has some advice about correcting a scoffer. Let's read Proverbs 9:7 and 8.
c3-pro-0002: Wisdom was there before the mountains were settled, when the LORD prepared the heavens. Read Proverbs 8:27 and 30 with me.
c3-pro-0003: Wisdom and Folly both call out, "Whoever is simple, let him turn in here." Let's read Proverbs 9:16, 9:18, and 8:35.
c1-dan-0017: In the middle of Belshazzar's great feast, something suddenly appeared on the plaster of the palace wall. Let's go to Daniel 5:5.
c2-dan-0001: Nebuchadnezzar demanded that his wise men tell him both his dream and what it meant. Let's read Daniel 2:10 and 11.
c2-dan-0002: A decree went out to destroy the wise men, so Daniel went home and told Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Let's look closely at Daniel 2:17 and 18.
c2-dan-0003: In the king's dream, a stone cut out without hands struck the great image on its feet. Let's read Daniel 2:34 and 35.
c2-dan-0004: A watcher came down from heaven and cried, "Chop down the tree." Let's look at Daniel 4:14 and 17 together.
c2-dan-0005: The wall read MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN, and TEKEL meant weighed in the balances. Let's read Daniel 5:25 and 27.
c3-dan-0001: When the secret was made known to Daniel, he blessed God. Let's open Daniel 2:20 and 23.
c3-dan-0002: Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven, and his understanding returned. Let's read Daniel 4:34, 4:37, and 5:22.
c1-jer-0001: Jeremiah's book opens with the word of the LORD coming to a young man. Let's turn to Jeremiah 1:4 and 5.
c2-jer-0001: At the potter's house, a clay vessel was marred in the potter's hand. Let's read Jeremiah 18:3 and 4.
c2-jer-0002: The LORD told Jeremiah to take a scroll and write down all the words He had spoken. Let's check Jeremiah 36:2 and 4.
c2-jer-0003: Jeremiah was let down with ropes into a dungeon with nothing but mire. Let's read Jeremiah 38:7 and 9.
c2-jer-0004: When the LORD called, Jeremiah protested that he could not speak. Let's dig into Jeremiah 1:6 and 9.
c2-jer-0005: Jeremiah's letter to the captives speaks of the LORD's plans to give them a future and a hope. Let's read Jeremiah 29:10 and 11.
c3-jer-0001: The LORD told the exiles, "I will be found by you." Read Jeremiah 29:12, 13, and 14 with me.
c3-jer-0002: King Jehoiakim cut up the scroll and burned it, yet the words were written down again. Let's read Jeremiah 36:23, 36:32, and 31:33.
c1-jer-0002: The LORD sent Jeremiah to stand in the gate of His house and speak to the people of Judah. Let's go to Jeremiah 7:2 and 4.
c2-jer-0006: Some people did evil and then came to stand before the LORD in the house called by His name. Let's read Jeremiah 7:10 and 11.
c2-jer-0007: Jeremiah went to the Potsherd Gate with a potter's earthen flask and some of the elders. Let's look closely at Jeremiah 19:10 and 11.
c2-jer-0008: Jeremiah was mocked daily and said he would not speak anymore in the LORD's name. Let's read Jeremiah 20:8 and 9.
c2-jer-0009: Jeremiah wore a yoke as the LORD's sign, and Hananiah took it off him in front of the people. Let's look at Jeremiah 28:10 and 13 together.
c2-jer-0010: Jeremiah warned the captives in Babylon not to be fooled by the prophets and diviners among them. Let's read Jeremiah 29:7 and 8.
c3-jer-0003: The LORD asks if He is only a God near at hand and not a God afar off. Let's open Jeremiah 23:23 and 24.
c3-jer-0004: False prophets kept promising good news, and Hananiah announced that Babylon's yoke had ended. Let's read Jeremiah 23:17, 28:2, and 28:9.
c1-ezk-0001: Ezekiel was a priest among the captives, and he saw visions of God. Let's turn to Ezekiel 1:1 and 3.
c2-ezk-0001: Ezekiel saw the likeness of the glory of the LORD. Let's read Ezekiel 1:28.
c2-ezk-0002: The LORD told Ezekiel to prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Let's check Ezekiel 34:2 and 3.
c2-ezk-0003: In a valley full of very dry bones, the LORD asked, "Son of man, can these bones live?" Let's read Ezekiel 37:2 and 3.
c2-ezk-0004: Ezekiel prophesied, and with a rattling the bones came together, bone to bone. Let's dig into Ezekiel 37:7 and 10.
c2-ezk-0005: The LORD said He was against the shepherds and would deliver His flock from them. Let's read Ezekiel 34:10 and 11.
c3-ezk-0001: The LORD promised to sprinkle clean water on His people and cleanse them. Read Ezekiel 36:25 and 26 with me.
c3-ezk-0002: Twice the LORD promises, "I will put My Spirit" in His people. Let's read Ezekiel 36:27 and 37:14.
c1-ezk-0002: As the LORD began Ezekiel's commission, He called him "Son of man." Let's go to Ezekiel 2:1 and 2.
c2-ezk-0006: The LORD sent Ezekiel to a rebellious house, whether they would hear or refuse. Let's read Ezekiel 2:5 and 7.
c2-ezk-0007: A hand held out a scroll full of lamentations and mourning and woe. Let's look closely at Ezekiel 3:1 and 2.
c2-ezk-0008: Israel had a proverb about sour grapes and teeth set on edge. Let's read Ezekiel 18:2 and 4.
c2-ezk-0009: A watchman sees the sword coming and blows the trumpet to warn the people. Let's look at Ezekiel 33:3 and 5 together.
c2-ezk-0010: The LORD told Ezekiel the house of Israel would not listen to him. Let's read Ezekiel 3:7 and 9.
c3-ezk-0003: Twice the house of Israel complained, "The way of the Lord is not fair." Let's open Ezekiel 18:25 and 29.
c3-ezk-0004: The LORD made Ezekiel a watchman to warn the wicked to turn from his way. Let's read Ezekiel 33:7, 33:9, and 18:32.
c1-luk-0036: Zacharias the priest was serving before God when the lot fell to him in the temple. Let's turn to Luke 1:8 and 9.
c2-luk-0005: The relatives wanted to name the baby after his father, so they made signs to Zacharias. Let's read Luke 1:62 and 63.
c2-luk-0006: Mary's song praises God for great reversals, the mighty and the lowly, the hungry and the rich. Let's check Luke 1:52 and 53.
c2-mat-0012: Matthew opens with the book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the Son of David. Let's read Matthew 1:1.
c2-luk-0007: The Holy Spirit had told Simeon he would see the Lord's Christ before he died, and then he held the Child. Let's dig into Luke 2:26 and 30.
c2-luk-0008: Anna, a widow of about eighty-four, served God in the temple night and day. Let's read Luke 2:37 and 38.
c3-mat-0001: Matthew sums up the genealogy in three sets of fourteen generations. Read Matthew 1:11, 12, and 17 with me.
c3-luk-0001: Zacharias asked the angel, "How shall I know this?" and Mary received an angel's message too. Let's read Luke 1:18, 20, and 45.
c1-mat-0035: Jesus asked His disciples, "Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?" Let's go to Matthew 16:13.
c2-mat-0013: As John's disciples left, Jesus asked the crowds what they had gone out into the wilderness to see. Let's read Matthew 11:9 and 10.
c2-mat-0014: Jesus asked, "But who do you say that I am?" Let's hear Simon Peter in Matthew 16:15 and 16.
c2-mat-0015: On the high mountain, Peter said, "Lord, it is good for us to be here." Let's look closely at Matthew 17:4.
c2-mat-0016: Jesus was transfigured on a high mountain, and His face shone like the sun. Let's read Matthew 17:2 and 3.
c2-mat-0017: The disciples heard the voice from the cloud and fell on their faces. Let's look at Matthew 17:6 and 7 together.
c3-mat-0002: A voice from the bright cloud told the disciples to hear the Beloved Son. Let's read Matthew 17:5 and 8.
c3-mat-0003: From prison, John sent to ask Jesus, "Are You the Coming One?" Let's open Matthew 11:3, 11:4, and 16:17.
c1-mrk-0022: Jesus spoke openly about suffering, being killed, and rising again after three days. Let's read Mark 8:31 and 32.
c2-mrk-0002: A father brought his son to Jesus, who said, "All things are possible to him who believes." Let's turn to Mark 9:23 and 24.
c2-mrk-0003: In a house at Capernaum, Jesus set a little child in the midst of the twelve. Let's read Mark 9:36 and 37.
c2-mrk-0004: A man told Jesus he had kept all the commandments since his youth. Let's check Mark 10:20 and 21.
c2-mrk-0005: The man went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions. Let's read Mark 10:22 and 25.
c2-mrk-0006: A scribe agreed that loving God and neighbor is more than all the offerings and sacrifices. Let's dig into Mark 12:33 and 34.
c3-mrk-0001: Many rich people put in much, and one poor widow put in two mites. Let's read Mark 12:42, 43, and 44.
c3-mrk-0002: The disciples argued about who was the greatest, and James and John asked for seats in His glory. Read Mark 9:35, 10:37, and 10:43 with me.
c1-jhn-0032: Before the Feast of the Passover, Jesus rose from supper and laid aside His garments. Let's read John 13:4 and 5.
c2-jhn-0011: Jesus came to wash Simon Peter's feet, and Peter was startled. Let's go to John 13:6 and 8.
c2-jhn-0012: Jesus said, "Let not your heart be troubled," and spoke of many mansions in His Father's house. Let's read John 14:1 and 2.
c2-jhn-0013: Jesus said, "And where I go you know, and the way you know." Let's look closely at John 14:4 and 5.
c2-jhn-0014: Jesus told His disciples, "Abide in Me, and I in you." Let's read John 15:4 and 5.
c2-jhn-0015: Jesus said, "You are My friends if you do whatever I command you." Let's look at John 15:14 and 15 together.
c3-jhn-0001: In His prayer in John 17, Jesus asks the Father for the same thing three times. Let's read John 17:11, 21, and 22.
c3-jhn-0002: Jesus loved His own to the end and prayed that the Father's love would be in them. Let's open John 13:1, 15:12, and 17:26.
c1-act-0031: The number of disciples was multiplying, and the Hellenists brought a complaint against the Hebrews. Let's read Acts 6:1.
c2-act-0010: The twelve asked the disciples to seek out seven men of good reputation for a job. Let's turn to Acts 6:3 and 4.
c2-act-0011: False witnesses told the council that Stephen spoke against the holy place and the law. Let's read Acts 6:13 and 15.
c2-act-0012: After his speech, Stephen gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God. Let's check Acts 7:55 and 56.
c2-act-0013: Cornelius gave generously to the people and prayed to God always. Let's read Acts 10:2 and 4.
c2-act-0014: Some in Jerusalem challenged Peter for eating with uncircumcised men, and then he explained what happened. Let's dig into Acts 11:3 and 11:18.
c3-act-0001: Some from Jerusalem had troubled the Gentile believers, so the council wrote them a letter. Let's read Acts 15:24 and 28.
c3-act-0002: A voice told Peter, "What God has cleansed you must not call common." Read Acts 10:15, 10:28, and 15:9 with me.
c1-rom-0017: Romans 8 opens with a word about those who are in Christ Jesus. Let's read Romans 8:1.
c2-rom-0002: Paul says believers did not receive the spirit of bondage again to fear. Let's go to Romans 8:15.
c2-rom-0003: Sometimes we do not know what to pray for as we ought. Let's read Romans 8:26.
c2-rom-0004: Paul asks, "What then shall we say to these things?" Let's look closely at Romans 8:31.
c2-rom-0005: The Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. Let's read Romans 8:16 and 17.
c2-rom-0006: Paul urges believers to present their bodies to God and not be conformed to this world. Let's look at Romans 12:1 and 2 together.
c3-rom-0001: Paul puts the sufferings of this present time on the scale. Let's read Romans 8:17 and 18.
c3-rom-0002: Tribulation, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, peril, sword: Paul names them all. Let's open Romans 8:28, 35, and 37.
c1-1co-0008: The Corinthians were lining up behind leaders: "I am of Paul," "I am of Apollos." Let's read First Corinthians 1:12 and 13.
c2-1co-0002: To those who are perishing, the message of the cross is foolishness. Let's turn to First Corinthians 1:18.
c2-1co-0003: Paul could not speak to the Corinthians as spiritual people, only as babes in Christ. Let's read First Corinthians 3:1 and 2.
c2-1co-0004: Paul weighs a handful of words against ten thousand words in a tongue. Let's check First Corinthians 14:19.
c2-1co-0005: Paul tells the Corinthians they are the temple of God, and that temple is holy. Let's read First Corinthians 3:16 and 17.
c2-1co-0006: Knowledge puffs up, but love edifies, and a weak brother can be harmed. Let's dig into First Corinthians 8:1 and 13.
c3-1co-0001: When the Corinthians gathered, some went hungry while others were drunk. Let's read First Corinthians 11:21 and 33.
c3-1co-0002: Paul pleads for no divisions, and he says God is not the author of confusion but of peace. Read First Corinthians 1:10, 14:33, and 14:40 with me.
c1-gal-0009: After God revealed His Son in him, Paul did not go straight up to Jerusalem. Let's read Galatians 1:16 and 17.
c2-gal-0002: Paul says the gospel he preached was not according to man. Let's go to Galatians 1:11 and 12.
c2-gal-0003: James, Cephas, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship. Let's read Galatians 2:9 and 10.
c2-gal-0004: Before faith came, Paul says, we were kept under guard by the law. Let's look closely at Galatians 3:23 and 24.
c2-gal-0005: Neither Jew nor Greek, neither slave nor free, neither male nor female. Let's read Galatians 3:26 and 28.
c2-gal-0006: When the fullness of the time had come, God acted. Let's look at Galatians 4:4 and 7 together.
c3-gal-0001: Paul tells the Galatians to stand fast in the liberty Christ won for them. Let's read Galatians 5:1 and 6.
c3-gal-0002: Abraham believed God, and the law came four hundred and thirty years later. Let's open Galatians 3:6, 17, and 18.
c1-2co-0001: Paul says, "But we have this treasure." Let's read Second Corinthians 4:7.
c2-2co-0001: Paul pairs each hardship with what did not happen. Let's turn to Second Corinthians 4:8 and 9.
c2-2co-0002: "Therefore we do not lose heart," Paul says, even as our outward man is perishing. Let's read Second Corinthians 4:16.
c2-2co-0003: Paul writes about anyone who is in Christ. Let's check Second Corinthians 5:17.
c2-2co-0004: God has reconciled us to Himself and given us the ministry of reconciliation. Let's read Second Corinthians 5:18 and 20.
c2-2co-0005: Paul compares giving to sowing: sow sparingly, reap sparingly. Let's dig into Second Corinthians 9:6 and 7.
c3-2co-0001: Paul calls our affliction light, working for us an eternal weight of glory. Let's read Second Corinthians 4:17 and 18.
c3-2co-0002: The Lord told Paul, "My strength is made perfect in weakness," and Paul chose to boast in his infirmities. Read Second Corinthians 4:7, 12:9, and 12:10 with me.
c1-2ti-0001: Paul remembers something genuine in Timothy that dwelt first in his grandmother and his mother. Let's read Second Timothy 1:5.
c2-2ti-0001: Paul thought about what was genuine in Timothy, and then he gave him a reminder. Let's go to Second Timothy 1:5 and 6.
c2-2ti-0002: God has not given us a spirit of fear. Let's read Second Timothy 1:7.
c2-2ti-0003: Paul tells Timothy to be diligent, a worker approved by God who does not need to be ashamed. Let's look closely at Second Timothy 2:15.
c2-2ti-0004: Paul tells Timothy to continue in what he has learned, remembering the Holy Scriptures he knew from childhood. Let's read Second Timothy 3:14 and 15.
c2-2ti-0005: All Scripture is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness. Let's look at Second Timothy 3:16 and 17 together.
c3-2ti-0001: Paul says he is being poured out as a drink offering, and a crown is laid up for him. Let's read Second Timothy 4:6 and 8.
c3-2ti-0002: Paul remembers Timothy's grandmother and mother, and then he looks back over his own life. Let's open Second Timothy 1:5, 3:15, and 4:7.
c1-1pe-0001: Peter opens with praise to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. Let's read First Peter 1:3.
c2-1pe-0001: Peter describes an inheritance that is incorruptible, undefiled, and does not fade away. Let's turn to First Peter 1:4.
c2-1pe-0002: Peter writes about loving Jesus without having seen Him. Let's read First Peter 1:8.
c2-1pe-0003: Peter says to always be ready when someone asks you for a reason. Let's check First Peter 3:15.
c2-1pe-0004: Peter calls believers a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation. Let's read First Peter 2:9 and 10.
c2-1pe-0005: Peter tells believers to humble themselves under God's mighty hand and cast all their worries on Him. Let's dig into First Peter 5:6 and 7.
c3-1pe-0001: Peter warns that the devil walks about like a roaring lion, and this lion knows the difference. Let's read First Peter 5:8 and 9.
c3-1pe-0002: Peter says various trials test the genuineness of our faith. Read First Peter 1:6, 1:7, and 5:9 with me.
c1-1jn-0001: John passes along the message he heard from Him. Let's read First John 1:5.
c2-1jn-0001: John writes about what happens when we confess our sins. Let's go to First John 1:9.
c2-1jn-0002: John says it has not yet been revealed what we shall be. Let's read First John 3:2.
c2-1jn-0003: John tells us the reason we love Him. Let's look closely at First John 4:19.
c2-1jn-0004: John explains why some do not know God, and then he says it again. Let's read First John 4:8 and 16.
c2-1jn-0005: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. Let's look at First John 5:11 and 13 together.
c3-1jn-0001: John says that if we claim to be close to Him but do not practice the truth, we lie. Let's read First John 1:6 and 7.
c3-1jn-0002: John talks about God sending His Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Let's open First John 4:7, 10, and 18.
